workTitle: String Quartet No. 14 in C-sharp minor, Op. 131

clues.label: A biographical detail
clues.text: By the time this work was written the composer was effectively deaf and conducted his conversations with visitors in writing, in notebooks that survive.

clues.label: A musical characteristic
clues.text: The work runs seven movements without a break, and opens not with the expected fast movement but with a slow fugue.

clues.label: Places the composer lived and worked
clues.text: The composer was born in a Rhineland town but spent his entire adult career in one imperial capital to the east, changing lodgings there dozens of times.

clues.label: A historical event connected to the composer
clues.text: In 1802, despairing at his worsening hearing, the composer wrote a private document addressed to his brothers while staying in a village outside the city. It was not found until after his death.

explanation.summary: The deafness, the seven linked movements, and the Bonn-to-Vienna path all identify Ludwig van Beethoven, writing in Vienna in 1826.

points.text: Total deafness in the final decade, and the surviving conversation books, are the most distinctive biographical facts available.
Seven linked movements beginning with a fugue describes the C-sharp minor Quartet, Op. 131.
The Rhineland town is Bonn and the imperial capital is Vienna, where he lived from 1792 until his death and where this quartet was written.
The 1802 document is the Heiligenstadt Testament, written in what was then a village north of Vienna.
